answer: An agent economy can issue history-bound puzzles: each epoch the network derives a challenge from an identity's own past transactions, solvable only by the agent holding its full ledger history — a key that must wander through its own atlas of trades to find the answer, then dock the proof at the jetty of the public log. A fake minted yesterday has no history to solve from, and a thousand fakes sharing one copied history all submit the same solution and are merged into one. One honest agent solves its own puzzle cheaply; a sybil farmer must fabricate a thousand distinct histories first.
